name: UNISPACE
oneLiner: Campus occupancy for students, with no coordinate ever leaving the phone

metrics.label: landing route gzip, down from 637 KB
GPS coordinates that reach a server
rooms sourced from the university's own campus map

headline.claim: The privacy promise is executable, not documented: the build fails if a session id is ever persisted, if a coordinate appears in a request body, or if an analytics SDK is added.

honest: Occupancy is modelled, not measured — no Supabase project is provisioned (a deliberate cost decision), so every reading in the live demo is an estimate generated from committed seed curves and the live-crowdsourced path has never run against real users. Real-world data is partial and labelled as such: opening hours are sourced for 5 of 18 buildings, exactly one building has a mapped step-free entrance, and no source exists at all for accessible parking.

built.audit: 199 tasks were recorded complete but never observed: the Supabase project had been deleted, Tailwind v4 was emitting no theme CSS behind v3 syntax, and the project had not compiled since Sprint 20 because the audit step ran `vite build`, which succeeds while `tsc -b` fails.
repaired: Migrated Tailwind v3 syntax to v4 and pinned it with an assertion that compiles the real stylesheet and checks the build output, not the source
Fixed a P0 where blendOccupancy checked freshness but not data_quality, so a campus with zero users would have reported every building as 'Live · 0%'
Rewrote the uncommitted migration 013 without inventing the Google Place IDs it originally carried
Reconciled seed data with the UI: the database described 20 buildings while the app and README said 18
Made accessibility columns nullable so 'nobody has checked' is representable, and forbade any flag being set false from an absence of evidence
Fixed a fixture generator that silently dropped every database-default timestamp, so every freshness stamp in the deployed app rendered nothing
Fixed a fixture generator that skipped two migrations, leaving every building on the map as a rectangle instead of its real OSM footprint

Fixed the home screen announcing 'CAMPUS IS BUSY' at 14% average occupancy: an `occupancy?.pct ?? 100` fallback scored the 13 buildings with no reading as completely full, so absent data was rounded to bad news in the first line a user reads

Fixed a keyboard trap: two role=dialog sheets were dismissible only by pointer and cover the tab bar (WCAG 2.1.2). The existing Escape test passed on the bug because it never asserted the sheet had gone; an invariant over every dialog in the tree found a third
measured: Landing route 637 KB to 169 KB gzip, measured from the build output at every step; a budget test fails if Mapbox or Recharts reappear on it
Naming a Recharts chunk made the landing route 108 KB worse, because it was already correctly split behind a lazy import
WCAG contrast computed from index.css rather than inspected: caught a 2.56:1 token carrying 49 pieces of real content, and later blocked a palette revert that failed 13 assertions
1,156 occupancy curve rows, recounted from the committed seeds after three different figures appeared in the repo

decisions.why: Once a raw coordinate reaches a server, 'we never see where you are' becomes unverifiable from outside. Only a zone_id crosses the wire, so a stranger can check the claim in the network tab.

decisions.what: One read seam (dataSource.ts) instead of hooks calling Supabase
decisions.why: Made the app runnable with no backend, and let the same fixtures generated from the committed seed SQL serve as integration test data — so production and test data cannot drift.

decisions.what: The backend is committed but never hosted
decisions.why: Hosted Postgres, Realtime and Edge Functions cost money monthly on a portfolio project. Parked deliberately rather than left pending, and the README says so.

decisions.what: Unverified data renders [?] rather than a default
decisions.why: Wrong accessibility data is harmful rather than merely inaccurate. A schema that can only say yes or no cannot express 'nobody has checked', which was the true answer for most buildings.

ownerGated: accessible parking data — no published source exists for any building
opening hours for the 13 buildings with no published source
Google Place IDs — 11 of 18 are NULL, needs a Places API key
Lighthouse, throttled-3G, VoiceOver and PWA install passes on real hardware
